SA01.why: Bakery receipts: classify a given pair of price equations (inconsistent). SA01 asks which new fact makes the system determined. Different ask. Cited.
Constants that make a system dependent. SA01 runs the idea in reverse (spot the disguised multiples). Allowed.
3 roses + 4 tulips = $27 and 9 roses + k tulips = $81 are 'not enough': find k. Same dependence idea with a constant; different ask.

SA02.why: Not cited by the generator. 000300: Lena's savings 200 + 15w, Omar's 350 − 10w; least whole number of weeks for Lena's savings to be more than twice Omar's (15). SA02: Ana 200 + 35w, Ben 500 − 15w; first week Ana's savings are at least twice Ben's (13). Same mechanism (rising vs falling linear balance, 'twice', solve, round up to the next whole week), same asked quantity, even the same starting 200 and the same names pattern. Drop.
Cited. Equality of two linear quantities; writing an 'at least twice' inequality. Different ask.

SA03.why: Mixture with known concentrations. SA03 must first recover both concentrations from two trial mixtures. Different key step. Cited.
Blend two fertilizers to hit two nutrient targets (2x2 system). Different ask. Cited.
Evaporation and replacement mixtures. Different mechanism.

SA04.why: 15% off then a $6 coupon equals 80% of the original. Different structure (percent known). Cited.

SA05.why: Extreme x of a system of two inequalities, abstract. Cited.
Drone payload cap with at-least conditions; asks for a count of combinations. Different ask.
Greatest possible value under a fuel cap and an 'at least' reserve. Single variable; different structure.

SA06.why: Generator-cited but mis-adjudicated. 000274: C = 0.8m + 25 with m in minutes; by how much does the cost increase for each additional hour? (48 = 0.8 x 60). SA06: C = 2.4n + 50 with n in hundreds of flyers; by how much does the charge increase for each additional flyer? (0.024 = 2.4 / 100). Same mechanism (rescale the slope by the unit factor between the variable's unit and the asked unit) and the same asked quantity (increase per one of a different unit). The direction of the conversion (divide vs multiply) is a numbers change; the distractors are the same kinds (raw coefficient; wrong power of 10; intercept mixed in). Drop.
Rewrite an equation when items come in boxes of 24. Different ask. Cited.

SA06.other_id: ideas-gen-12 GC08 / ideas-gen-16 KC14 (both dropped, not banked)
SA06.why: Scaled-x slope on a best-fit line. Same family; see also SC01 in this set (within-list).

SA07.why: Generator-flagged. Adjudicated: close only. 000398 is a 2x2 system whose x-value does not depend on k (proportional rows). SA07 is one equation in one variable that factors as (c − 3)(x − 4) = 0, and the ask is the solution x. Same 'answer independent of the parameter' insight, different structure.

Not cited by the generator. (c − 4)x = c² − 16: value of c for infinitely many solutions. Same parameter-factoring structure (coefficient and constant share a factor of c − k), but it asks for c; SA07 asks for x once c ≠ 3. Allowed; cite it and keep it in a different batch.
No-solution constants; 'exactly one real solution, what is that solution' for a quadratic (discriminant). Different mechanism.

SA08.why: Per-use vs flat rate; average cost under two-tier pricing. Neither buys unused items. Cited.
Least whole number from a strict inequality. Generic rounding step only.

SA09.why: Not cited by the generator. ACT-100: the sum of two numbers is 30 and the larger is 3 more than twice the smaller; find the larger (21). SA09: total seats 1,200 and the balcony is 40 less than one-third of the main floor; find the balcony (270). Same mechanism (sum constraint plus 'k more/less than a multiple of the other', substitute, solve, report the dependent part) and the same asked quantity (the part defined by the relation). Only the multiple (1/3 vs 2), the sign and a seating context change; the traps are the same kinds (the other part; mis-grouped translation). Cross-exam re-skin: drop.
Single-statement translations with no total. Cited.

SA10.why: Not cited by the generator. 000352: linear f passes through (2, 9) and f(x) − 2x is the same for every x; find f(7) (19). SA10: linear f passes through (2, 5) and g(x) = f(x) + 3x has a horizontal graph (i.e., is constant); find f(0) (11). Same mechanism (adding/subtracting a linear term makes the function constant, which fixes the slope, then the point fixes the intercept) and same asked quantity (a value of f at another input; f(0) is just the intercept). 'Horizontal line' is a restatement of 'the same for every x'. Drop.
Cited. Shared point / vertical shift. Different mechanism.

SA11.why: Per-member amounts with fixed membership and a short/excess total. SA11 changes the number of people with an equal total. Different key step. Cited.
Bus $600 split equally; 10 more members, $5 less each; find members (rational equation). Same context family; SA11 has two scenarios and asks for the total via a linear system in c and n. Allowed.

SA12.why: Input whose output is the average of two outputs. Different ask. Cited.
No SAT item sums a run of function values (no arithmetic-series item found in sat_math.json). See scope note.

SA13.why: Generator-flagged. Adjudicated: close only. 000602 converts a given °F interval to °C through F = 1.8C + 32. SA13 forms the error of an approximation, (2C + 30) − (1.8C + 32) = 0.2C − 2, and bounds its absolute value. Same formula and the same answer form (a compound inequality in C), different key step. Keep in a different batch.
Generator-flagged. Miscalibrated linear reading compared with the truth, solved as an equation for one input. Different ask (one value vs an interval).

Tolerance family: |L − 80| ≤ 0.6 carried through a transformation; scale within 2% of truth; acceptable-length absolute-value inequality. None has the error as a linear function of the input that crosses zero. Allowed; do not batch with 000602, 000885 or 000492.

SA14.why: f(a) = b and f(b) = a; which must be true (slope −1, f(0) = a + b). Linear f through parameter points; different ask. Cited. Keep in a different batch from batch-079 items.
Not cited. f(0) = 10, f(3) = k, f(k) = 3; find k. Parameter points again; different ask.
Slope 3 through (a, b) and (b, a + 6); find b − a. Cited.

SA15.why: Generator-cited but mis-described: the generator says 000048 'reads a table with unit steps'. It does not. 000048: the table gives f at x = 2, 5, 9 (11, 20, 32), steps of 3 and 4; find f(−4). SA15: the cost at 2, 5, 9 notebooks (9.50, 17.00, 27.00), steps of 3 and 4; find the fixed charge (the value at 0). Same x-values, same mechanism (slope from non-unit steps, then extrapolate outside the table), and the same asked quantity (a value of the linear function at an input not in the table; the intercept is f(0)). Only the outputs and a store context change. Drop.
Caterer fixed fee plus per-guest cost from two events; asks a later cost after a 10% change. Different ask.
m + b from two values. Cited.

SC01.why: Change in x for a given change in predicted y; no unit scaling. Cited. Keep apart from batch-075.
Not cited. Slope times a unit factor (per minute to per hour). SC01 adds the scaled x (thousands) and a best-fit context, and asks for a predicted difference. Same family, different ask.

Scaled-x best-fit slope applied to a raw-unit change. KC14 was dropped as a template of GC08, and GC08 was dropped at drafting (key cue, implausible slope), so neither is banked; SC01 is the only live member of this family and may go ahead. Mention them in the provenance notes.
Best-fit equation after rewriting y in cents. Cited.

SC02.why: Choose the best line for 4 points with unit spacing. Cited.
Not cited. Table with x = 0, 1, 2, 3; linear or exponential with the slope/factor. SC02's unequal x-spacing is the new step. Allowed.
Linear vs exponential model through two given points. Different ask.

SC03.why: Not cited by the generator. ACT-295: 200 of 1,000 people have a condition; a test is positive for 90% of those with it and 10% of those without; given a positive result, P(has the condition) = 9/13. SC03: box A (20 bulbs, 15% defective) and box B (40 bulbs, 10% defective); given defective, P(from box A) = 3/7. Same mechanism (turn two rates on two bases of different sizes into counts, then condition on the shared outcome) and the same asked quantity (P(source | outcome)); the distractors are the same kinds (the reverse conditional 9/10 vs 3/20; the base share 1/5 vs 1/3). Cross-exam re-skin: drop.
Same 'condition on the outcome' ask but with counts given (no rates).
Cited. Unequal class sizes, no condition; rooms chosen with equal probability.

SC04.why: Bounds the median of two combined lists from their medians. Cited.

One frequency table; least frequency for a median of 3. Cited.

What a random-sample association supports. Cited.

Turnout percents to counts. Different ask.
Mean needed on remaining tests. Same 'what is needed on the rest' family, but with means, not a percent of a new base. Allowed.

Two-way table conditional probability. Different construction.

SC09.why: Subset sums of a mean. Cited.
Median and mean constraints on a list; extreme value of one element. Different ask.

SC15.why: Generator-flagged. Adjudicated: template (cross-exam). ACT-387: A is 25% more than B; B is what percent less than A (20%). SC15, after the shared 20% sale cancels: the member price is 10% less than the nonmember price; the nonmember price is what percent greater than the member price (11.1%). Same mechanism (switch the base of a single percent comparison, 1/0.9 − 1) and the same asked quantity (the percent difference measured on the other base); only the direction and the numbers change, and the distractors are the same kind (the original percent on the wrong base). The 20% sale is a given number that turns out irrelevant (a cue the generator advertises as the 'twist'). Drop.

Generator-flagged. Two chained comparisons with changing bases (C is what percent greater than A, 14.3%). SC15 reduces to one comparison; close only, but the same 'approximately what percent greater' wording and answer form. If SC15 is kept anyway, never batch it with 000886.

within_list_cues.SA01: Odd-one-out cue: the key is the only fact stated as a difference ('$300 more than'); B, C and D are all 'a per-item amount on each, N in all' totals. A test-taker who expects the odd choice to be right picks A without testing dependence. Rewrite the key as a total of the same shape that is independent, e.g. 'Folding each shirt took 2 minutes and each hat took 3 minutes, 170 minutes in all' (2x + 3y = 170 gives x = 40, y = 30; checked), and move the time-based dependent fact to another distractor form, or make one distractor a difference-type fact that is also dependent-looking.
within_list_cues.SA02: Trap rationale error: '20, doubling Ana's side' is wrong. 2(200 + 35w) ≥ 500 − 15w gives 85w ≥ 100, w ≥ 1.18, i.e. 2. Moot (drop).
within_list_cues.SA05: Distractors C (29) and D (42) are eliminable by common sense: the lighter of two bags with a combined weight of at most 50 kg can never exceed 25 kg, so only A and B survive. Replace them with values ≤ 25, e.g. 25 (ignores the 8-kg condition, 50/2) and a second plausible slip below 25.
within_list_cues.SA07: Mild: the answer 4 is visible in c(x − 4), and plugging x = 4 makes c vanish, so a student can guess 4 without the 'exactly one solution' reasoning. Acceptable for SPR, but consider writing the equation expanded, e.g. cx + 12 = 3x + 4c.
within_list_cues.SA08: Key guessable without the math: n must be less than 12 and the answer is the least qualifying n, but only n = 11 qualifies (10.4 threshold), so the answer is simply the largest allowed value. Change the group price so that several n qualify, e.g. $11 per ticket: 132 < 15n, n > 8.8, answer 9 (traps 8, 8.8, 12, 4).
within_list_cues.SA12: Calculator shortcut: with f(x) = 3x + 1 found, eleven values can be summed directly; that is acceptable (it is the math), but note the item is easier than 'medium-hard' for a calculator user.
within_list_cues.SA13: Plugging in the endpoints 0 and 20 and one negative value eliminates every distractor; this is legitimate checking for an interval item, not a defect. No length or wording cue.
within_list_cues.SA14: Test value a = 1 (f(1) = 2, f(2) = 3, so f(5) = 6) eliminates every distractor. Acceptable: the choices are expressions in a, so this is an identity-type item.
within_list_cues.SA15: The third table row is redundant (any two rows fix the line). Moot (drop).
within_list_cues.SC05: Key D is clearly the longest choice and the only hedged one ('plausibly close to'). Shorten D (e.g. 'Sampling variability explains the differences; the population mean is likely near 7 hours') and lengthen one distractor, or hedge one distractor as well.
within_list_cues.SC10: Key D is clearly the longest choice (it repeats the stem and adds 'such as motivation'). Trim D to about the length of A and C.
within_list_cues.SC11: C and D give the same average rate (12 L/min); harmless for 'greatest', but a careful student may notice that two choices tie and are both wrong. Optional: change one value (e.g. 600 → 615 at t = 45, rate 13) to avoid the tie.
within_list_cues.SC13: The trap list gives 1.8 twice with two different rationales (the meeting time; scaling 1.2 by 3/2 once). Keep one rationale.
within_list_cues.SC15: Given number that turns out irrelevant: the 20% sale cancels, which the generator presents as the twist. Moot (drop).
within_list_cues.within-list: Same-family pairs inside set 24 to keep in different batches: SA06 and SC01 (unit-scaled slope; SA06 dropped anyway); SA10, SA12, SA14 and SA15 (linear function from two values); SA02 and SA08 (least whole number from a strict or non-strict inequality); SC03 and SC08 (conditional probability); SC04 and SC09 (median); SC06 and SC14 (percents with different bases); SC11, SC12 and SC13 (rates).

math_errors.SA02: Trap '20, doubling Ana's side instead of Ben's' is wrong: 2(200 + 35w) ≥ 500 − 15w gives w ≥ 20/17, so 2, not 20. (Other near readings give 16 or 23, never 20.) Moot because SA02 is dropped.
math_errors.SA11: Trap '180, the cost if the 30n terms are mishandled' has no reproducible derivation; replace it with a trap that comes from a stated error (e.g. 90 or 4 are already listed) or remove it.
